s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent lateral knee pain with an intra-articular space-occupying lesion
salient_findings: Recurrent pain localized to the lateral side of the left knee
Intra-articular space-occupying lesion invading the tibial plateau on MRI
Lesion with heterogeneous appearance on T2-weighted images and peripheral rim enhancement on gadolinium-enhanced MRI
key_facts: 30-year-old Asian man
6-month history of recurrent pain
Pain localized to the lateral side of the left knee
Slight tenderness and swelling over the lateral joint line
Plain radiographs were unremarkable
Routine laboratory tests were within normal limits
MRI demonstrated a 1.5 cm intra-articular space-occupying lesion
Lesion invaded the tibial plateau
Lesion was homogeneous and isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images
Lesion appeared heterogeneous with internal specks on T2-weighted images
Gadolinium-enhanced MRI showed enhancement confined to the peripheral rim of the mass
No satellite lesions identified

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor of bone
shortlist.why_kept: Common cause of intra-articular space-occupying lesions in the knee

shortlist.label: Chondroblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Typically presents with pain and swelling, and can have a similar appearance on MRI

shortlist.label: Pigmented villonodular synovitis
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause recurrent pain and swelling, and may have a heterogeneous appearance on MRI

shortlist.label: Synovial chondromatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause intra-articular space-occupying lesions and has a similar demographic profile

shortlist.label: Chondrosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although rare, it is a possible cause of an intra-articular space-occupying lesion with aggressive features

raw.rationale: The patient's age, location of the pain, and the appearance of the lesion on MRI are consistent with chondroblastoma, which is a rare type of bone tumor that typically affects the epiphyses of long bones in young adults and can extend into the metaphysis, including the tibial plateau.

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor of bone
rejected.why: Giant cell tumors are more common in older adults and typically have a more aggressive appearance on imaging, with a soap-bubble appearance and cortical expansion.

rejected.label: Pigmented villonodular synovitis
rejected.why: Pigmented villonodular synovitis typically presents with diffuse synovial involvement and multiple nodules, which is not consistent with the focal lesion described in this case.

rejected.label: Synovial chondromatosis
rejected.why: Synovial chondromatosis typically presents with multiple small cartilaginous nodules within the joint, which is not consistent with the single large lesion described in this case.

rejected.label: Chondrosarcoma
rejected.why: Chondrosarcomas are more common in older adults and typically have a more aggressive appearance on imaging, with cortical destruction and soft tissue extension, which is not consistent with the findings in this case.
